question: The task label matches (MCI vs healthy controls) but the channel does not: P-117 uses resting-state EEG; P-58 (Gosztolya et al., Computer Speech & Language 69 (2021) 101215) uses temporal parameters of spontaneous speech. Condition 1 fails on channel. Note: the round-20 reading could not check P-117 because the pack PDF is the wrong paper; this reading used the correct PDF (S1746809423008959, Aljalal et al., BSPC 87 (2024) 105462, DOI 10.1016/j.bspc.2023.105462), whose content matches the summaries.md Paper 117 block (the block header's file name S1746809423005462 does not exist in downloads/ and appears to fuse the PII with the article number).
metric: Accuracy in both once P-58's printed accuracies are used. The record's '67-92% range' is not an accuracy: it spans accuracy, precision, recall and specificity across feature subsets.

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-II channels; 99.51% all 19 channels), binary aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 segment feature vectors from 61 participants (29 aMCI/32 HC); no interval. Wilson 95% with n = 61: z^2/n = 0.06297; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06297 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-58: Accuracy at EER, SVM with nested leave-one-speaker-out CV (Table 3). English all features 84.8% (n = 33): centre (0.848 + 0.05820)/1.11641 = 0.8117, half-width 0.1215, Wilson [0.690, 0.933]. Hungarian all features 75.8% (n = 33): Wilson [0.590, 0.872]. Best accuracy 90.9% (Hungarian, filler-related subset, n = 33): z^2/n = 3.8415/33 = 0.11641; centre = (0.909 + 0.05820)/1.11641 = 0.8664; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.909*0.091/33 + 3.8415/(4*33^2))/1.11641 = 0.1022; Wilson [0.764, 0.969]. Printed accuracies range 39.4%-90.9%.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. Neither paper reports a result in the other's channel; P-117 prints only segment-level accuracies and P-58 only speaker-level ones. Nothing reconciles the pair.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% (>= 0.97), internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segment feature vectors, 61 participants, no external cohort (the round-20 reading's 'likely applies' is confirmed from the correct PDF). P-58's accuracies are all below 0.97; its best AUC is 0.932 (English all features); not excluded.
reason: Judged on the accuracies P-58 actually prints (condition 6 corrects the record's '67-92% range'), the gap is beyond uncertainty: 0.9981 lies outside every P-58 Wilson interval (highest upper bound 0.969) and each P-58 accuracy lies outside P-117's [0.937, 1.000]. But EEG and spontaneous speech are different measurement channels, so the pair fails condition 1, and P-117's 99.81% fails the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5).

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training
because we got quite similar scores (67-92%) as we did in the monolingual cases (67-92% as well).
Both the English-speaking (n = 33; New York, NY, USA) and the Hungarian-speaking (n = 33; Szeged, Hungary) participants were diagnosed as MCI or HC.
Besides an accuracy score of 84.8%, the recall/sensitivity and specificity values were also around 85%.
we achieved classification accuracy, recall (sensitivity) and specificity scores above 90%; with a precision score of 85.7%, it led to an F-measure value of 88.9.
